body: What do you mean by scale workers?  Do you increase the number of processes at runtime?

We run this in Docker containers on top of OpenShift, so by scale @fridex means running more containers (which means running more workers). To make the system more orchestrate-able and predictable on OpenShift we run with concurrency set to 1 in each container and scaling is left to OpenShift

Thanks for the explanation!

The issue has me scratching my head, as this `_quick_put` attribute is set only at startup, and I cannot see how it would be set to None any point later.

There are two branches in the worker: one threads based, another event loop based, and the
amqp/redis/sqs and qpid transports uses the event loop based one (unless you're on Windows).
This discusses only the event loop.
- The worker initializes the Pool by calling `pool = asynpool.Pool(concurrency)`
- When the event loop is started (also whenever the broker connection restarts), it calls `pool.register_with_event_loop(event_loop)`, which sets the _quick_put attribute to a closure.

So either it must be have never ben set, or it must fail in reaction to a connection being lost.  Did you see anything else in the logs before this happened?

It seems to me that this happens more often when we (yeah, I'm working on the same project as @vpavlin and @fridex :)) start new workers when some tasks are waiting to be processed. When we scale up if message queue is empty, much less (or even none) workers get stuck.
So this may have to do something with the initialization phase - maybe the celery process tries to grab a task and communicate with the worker subprocess before it's fully initialized?

Here's the complete log from a single failed worker from start until failing: https://paste.fedoraproject.org/469923/
The worker keeps running even after the traceback and shows up as active in celery flower.
Just to clarify, `SelinonTaskEnvelope` is from [Selinon](https://github.com/selinon). I suppose Selinon shouldn't affect this behaviour as this issue appears on Celery level.
So after recent tests, this issue occurs even with Celery 3.

I seem to be having the same issue, but only when listening on multiple queues. Did not experience this on celery 3.

Python 3.5.1
Django 1.10.2
celery 4.0.0
Broker: RabbitMQ
Not sure if this will help, but the worker does not crash if it's started in the background.

``` bash
$ QUEUES="q1,q2,q3,q4,q5,q6,q7,q8,q9"
$ celery worker -A project.foo -Q "$QUEUES" -l debug --concurrency=1 --prefetch-multiplier=1 -Ofair -D --logfile=celery.log
```

Still no success, I still see `quick_put` issue. Notably when a worker is connecting to RabbitMQ and there are tasks (cannot reproduce with empty queues). Tested with Celery 4.0.0rc6
@fridex As discussed, can you let me know what happens if you try using the `celery multi` method  ?

I confirm that when there is more queues and there are task in those queues then worker goes down.

I don't know if that helps, but I can get any information is necessary to resolve that bug (including as a last resort access to system where we have this problem). This is major problem for us right now.
+1. This forces us to to purge all queues every time we launch a new celery container. If celery starts with no messages in rabbitmq, then it works as expected.

@muhammedabad thanks for the suggestion, but the issue still persists:

Celery started as:

```
celery multi start myworker -A project.foo -Q "$QUEUES" -l debug --concurrency=1 --prefetch-multiplier=1 -Ofair --logfile=celery.log
```
